observation.visible_scene: A man in a light-blue shirt and patterned tie stands behind a dark glossy table in a room with a white projection screen and a wooden door. His right hand (viewer's left) is raised to about shoulder/face height, pinching a dark spherical ball between thumb and forefinger; his left hand rests flat on the table. A second identical dark ball sits stationary on the table to the viewer's right of him throughout.
visible_changes: For the first ~0.5 s the man holds the ball steady in his raised hand while his mouth is open (talking), with no ball motion.
Around t≈0.53–0.60 s the fingers open and the ball separates from the hand, beginning a downward fall.
From t≈0.60 s to t≈0.80 s the ball descends vertically past the tie and shirt, staying at roughly the same horizontal position, with motion blur visible near the bottom of the fall (t≈0.80 s).
By t≈0.83 s the ball has come to rest on the table surface at the viewer's left of the tie, and it remains stationary there through the end of the clip.
After releasing the ball the man's right hand stays raised in the same pinched posture and does not follow the ball down; his left hand remains on the table.
The man's mouth closes into a slight smile after the early talking frames.
The second ball on the viewer's-right side of the table never moves.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the ball was placed in the hand before t=0, and whether the man retrieves or moves it after the clip ends, are not shown.
The reason for the release (a deliberate drop vs. a slip) is not visible.
The acoustic/verbal context of the talking is unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact frame of release is between t≈0.50 s (still held) and t≈0.56 s (clearly falling).
The fall is essentially vertical; any horizontal drift of the ball is minimal and within pixel noise.
Background elements (screen, door) are fixed across frames, so no camera motion is detected, though small camera shifts cannot be fully excluded.
